highlight.title: What Actually Happens When You Type a URL and Press Enter
highlight.summary: Your browser performs a DNS lookup to find the server's IP address, establishes a secure connection, and fetches the webpage—all in under a second. Modern browsers now use encrypted DNS by default and HTTP/3 protocol for faster connections.

resources.title: Zero to Mastery: A Beginner's Guide to Computer Networking
resources.why_now: <cite index="4-19,4-20">The concept of a computer network might seem complex, but in reality, it's fundamentally quite straightforward. A computer network is just a group of computers and devices linked together in a way that allows them to communicate and share resources with each other.</cite> Perfect for teenagers getting started with networking fundamentals.

resources.title: What is DNS? The Complete 2026 Guide to How the Internet Works
resources.why_now: <cite index="11-28,11-29">DNS is the translator between human-friendly names and machine-friendly addresses. Without it, the internet would be a chaotic mess of numbers and zero websites would open by name.</cite> Understanding DNS is crucial as it's involved in every web request you make.

resources.title: Recent BGP Route Leak and Cloudflare Outage Analysis
resources.why_now: <cite index="23-2,23-3">An automated routing policy configuration error caused us to leak some Border Gateway Protocol prefixes unintentionally from a router at our Miami data center.</cite> Real-world examples like this show how internet infrastructure can break and affect millions of users.

resources.title: FreeCodeCamp: 12-Hour Computer Networking Deep Dive
resources.why_now: <cite index="10-4,10-5">For many technical jobs it is important to understand computer networking. We just posted a massive 12-hour course that will give you a deep dive into computer networking.</cite> Comprehensive technical resource covering IPv4, error control, flow control, and advanced networking concepts.

claude_take: The internet feels magical until it breaks—then you realize it's held together by protocols, routing tables, and the digital equivalent of traffic signs. Recent BGP incidents show how a single misconfigured router can take down major services worldwide, making these fundamentals more relevant than ever for understanding our interconnected world.
